Programmes are structured to give the borrower the means to finance its growth.&nbsp;</li><li><b>Off-balance sheet treatment: </b>deconsolidation can be negotiated in certain cases.<b>&nbsp;</b></li></ul>" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;align=left;spacingRight=8;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="40" y="190" width="300" height="310" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="DFV3-PLY_3wCLzb08eQx-4" value="<ul><li><b>Access to exposure types not available directly on the bond market</b> (e.g. exposure to mid-cap risk...)</li><li>The EU securitisation regulation offers a<b> transparent, effective framework for investors.</b></li><li><b>Attractive returns are available on mezzanine tranches.</b></li><li><b>Allows investment in relatively risky countries- </b>senior ABS tranches can be rated higher than the sovereign.&nbsp;</li></ul>" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;align=left;spacingRight=4;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="414" y="190" width="300" height="310" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="gZJBzyXn1qWZ3-shuHk7-2" value="<font color="#ffffff"><span style="font-size: 14px;">Advantages for originators</span></font>" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#76608A;strokeColor=#000000;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="44" y="110" width="296" height="60" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

ul.li: Cheaper than other forms of funding thanks to collateralisation and tranching of risk - provided that the portfolio securitised is large enough to absorb fixed costs (>EUR100M)

Access to investors which the originator would not be able to attract on a non-collateralised basis. Securitisation allows companies to raise funds from diversified sources: a banking pool, institutional investors, funds...
Flexible financing: the revolving nature of securitisation reduces the need for repetitive refinancing. Programmes are structured to give the borrower the means to finance its growth.
Off-balance sheet treatment: deconsolidation can be negotiated in certain cases.
